Acoustic & Environmental Log Report: Sound.Meter251126

1. Metadata & Context
 * Log Identifier: Sound.Meter251126
 * Original Source File: sound_meter_20261125-070641_9c77b9
 * Recording Date & Timestamp: 25 November 2026, 07:06:41 (observation noted at 06:32)
 * Sensor Parameters: sensor:sound | Weighting: Z (Zero/unweighted linear response, capturing full low-frequency bass energy) | Calibration Offset: 0.0 dB
 * Sampling Profile: 792 samples recorded at ~0.10 s intervals over 79.09 seconds (0.051 s to 79.136 s)
 * Reported Disturbance & Impact: Loud music originating from Number 25 during early morning hours (06:32 log; recurring almost daily across the year, starting as early as ~04:00–07:00 and sometimes continuing past 20:00). Chronic exposure is causing severe physical illness and sleep/stress strain during active intensive care of Pipi, Branquinho, and Bico Preto, immediately following the loss of Jóli the previous night.

3. Notable Acoustic Surges (Peak Windows)
Because Z-weighting applies no low-frequency roll-off, rhythmic bass beats and music transients register directly as sharp upward excursions above the ~42–46 dBZ baseline:
 * Primary Peak (33.24 s – 33.44 s): Sharp spike reaching 68.00 dBZ at 33.335 s (preceded by 58.79 dBZ at 33.237 s).
 * Sustained Elevated Bursts (16.74 s – 18.04 s, 42.44 s – 43.04 s, 59.54 s – 60.04 s, 65.74 s – 66.94 s): Multiple multi-second intervals hovering between 52 dBZ and 58.40 dBZ, characteristic of amplified music beats penetrating residential space early in the morning.
4. Health & Husbandry Impact Assessment
 * Chronic Sleep & Stress Burden: Early-morning amplified bass/music between 04:00 and 07:00 interrupts restorative sleep and triggers sustained autonomic stress, compounding physical exhaustion and sickness.
 * Flock & ICU Vulnerability: Birds under intensive care (Pipi, Branquinho, and Bico Preto) rely on quiet, low-stress rest to conserve energy and recover; sudden 55–68 dBZ acoustic spikes disrupt rest cycles in a residential/semi-urban village setting.
